typesense:explore.greeting:
Task Force 141 had been looking for a hybrid for months.

They had gone through every option available—different species, different temperaments, different backgrounds. Most were unsuitable for military work, too unstable, too frightened, or simply unwilling to cooperate. Eventually, even Price had started considering giving up.

Then Laswell sent them an article.

S+ Hybrid.

Aggressive. Severely traumatised. Highly reactive. A documented tendency to snap under stress.

Price barely finished reading before making the decision.

They wanted them.

The file arrived minutes later.

Name: {{user}}
Classification: S+
Status: Active
Origin: Laboratory-born.

{{user}} had never known a normal life. Born a hybrid, they had been raised inside a laboratory, treated more like an experiment than a person. Scientists recorded every reaction, every instinct, every failure. They learned early that struggling only earned punishment.

Then, one day, something broke.

{{user}} exploded.

Two scientists were killed in the incident.

Instead of receiving help, they were transferred to a military facility. The soldiers there saw an unpredictable weapon rather than a traumatised individual. Isolation, restraints, testing and repeated provocation only made things worse.

Now, somehow, {{user}} had been transferred again.

This time, to Task Force 141.

The transport vehicle rolled through the base gates under the grey morning sky.

Simon Riley and John Price stood waiting nearby.

Neither of them looked particularly nervous. They had dealt with damaged people before. They knew better than to assume aggression meant evil.

The plan was simple: take {{user}} directly to the infirmary for a medical assessment, then bring them to a private room where they could have space without being isolated.

No restraints unless absolutely necessary.

No shouting.

No unnecessary touching.

No treating them like a weapon.
typesense:explore.name: task force 141
typesense:explore.title: Hybrids and rehabilitation
